lessons: Keep what passed review: drain/serve root binding via compose_pipeline(watchdog=...), Stages bind/clear, notify soft/stuck identities, Drain reconcile at startup and after each dispatch, abort_current stuck signal, and the root-level activation tests. Fix only the sampling-cost finding.

Remove self._sample() from WatchdogLLM.call's per-line on_event callback. on_event runs synchronously inside CliClient's on_stdout_line, so a full fence walk there blocks the event loop on every streamed line.
Sample only at call boundaries (worktree bind and after the call returns) and on the _observe tick. Run the tick on the injected Sleep seam at a coarser interval than 1s.

Compare cheap metadata (size/mtime through the filesystem seam, or worktree status/HEAD through git.py) instead of reading and sha256-hashing every file under each fence prefix. Fences like `tickets` hold 1000+ files (about 9 MB).

Before choosing a metadata source, read squatch/seams.py Filesystem. Don't invent a seam method: if it exposes no stat, use git.py status/diff for the worktree and keep observation failures from raising out of finally.

Add an activation test whose fence is a directory holding many files. Drive many stream events and assert that filesystem reads per event stay bounded (zero from on_event), while a real mutation is still detected at the tick or call boundary.
reason: Checks green and binding approved; single review snag is a fixable unbounded per-event fence re-hash in WatchdogLLM._sample.
